cells.tense: You are at the fork where direction gets set, and the pen is in your hand.
cells.act: give a concrete piece of help and finish it
cells.ask: Hand one person the exact thing they need from what you carry — one introduction, one tool, one errand — and see it through to done. Close it out.
cells.core:
This part is working. You can tell which pull matters without arguing the case to yourself first, and you pass on what you have to the people walking the same way. What you hand out and what you keep do not compete here; both sit steady in the same hand.

Hand one person the exact thing they need from what you carry — one introduction, one tool, one errand — and see it through to done. The balance costs something to keep: sharing holds while there is something in reserve, so check what you are drawing on before you promise. Noticing that is how this stays a gift and not a drain.
cells.sheetLine: You can tell which pull matters and share what you have.

cells.tense: You have run ahead of the present, arranging a future that has not arrived yet.
cells.act: let several things be true and act on one
cells.ask: Let what is tugging at you sit side by side without ranking it — what you want, what someone else wants for you, what is only noise. Hold all of it, and act on none of it today.
cells.core:
Seeing the whole field of pulls at once and holding them until one rises is how you choose, and that part is sound. Trouble is that nothing in the field has been sorted yet: every lure, every crowd, every should reads as a direction, so much is being chosen that none of it lands anywhere.

Let several things be true at once and act on one later. Let what is tugging at you sit side by side without ranking — what you want, what someone else wants for you, what is only noise. Leave the page as it is. Letting the differences sit unforced is the work; nothing has to win today.
cells.sheetLine: Everything is pulling, so nothing gets picked.

cells.tense: You are waiting at a doorway you walked through some time back.
cells.act: take pleasure in the grown thing
cells.ask: Sit with something you have tended over the years and let it be good on its own, with no next step hanging off it. Stay as long as you like.
cells.core:
Going well, this part catches what matters before you can explain why, and points at it without strain. At the moment the pull to choose has gone quiet: everything ahead reads as a doorway already used up, and left is the flat sense that direction dried up somewhere behind.

Take pleasure in what you grew. Sit with something you have tended over the years — a skill, a body of work, a garden — and let it be good on its own, with no next step hanging off it. Not pushing a feeling into place; letting the grown thing be what it is. That is the small, honest move that refills this.
cells.sheetLine: The direction is behind you and the pull has gone quiet.

cells.tense: You are steering by a direction you set while the pen was down.
cells.act: share your strength where it is needed
cells.ask: Look for someone on the same road who is carrying more than you and put one piece of your strength into their hands — a lead, a tool, an open hour — then follow it to done.
cells.core:
The steering is happening. What is not happening is your name being on it. Whatever direction you set gets read as care for the group, or as just what you do with people, and the one doing the setting does not count it as theirs. The people alongside feel it hold. The one providing it files it under something else.

Look for someone on the same road who is carrying more than you and put one piece of your strength into their hands — a lead, a tool, an open hour — then follow it to done. That is the smaller version of doing what you already do, and this time you get to see the shape of it.
cells.sheetLine: The direction is yours and the credit for it isn't.
